detailed_rationale: YES BANK reported Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter) results on 18-Jul-2026 [DATA]: standalone PAT Rs.1,071cr (+34% YoY vs Rs.801cr), NII Rs.2,786cr (+17.5-18% YoY), NIM 2.7% (+20bps YoY) - still structurally the lowest among large private banks (peers ~4%+). Asset quality improved for another quarter: GNPA 1.3% (down from 1.6% YoY, flat vs Q4FY26's 1.3%), NNPA 0.2% (down from 0.3% YoY), PCR 81.7% [DATA]. But credit cost rose even as NPA ratios improved: provisions Rs.394cr, +38.9% YoY [DATA] - flag for forensic follow-up on provisioning mix (SR/AUCA-related vs fresh slippage recognition; not confirmed) [INFERENCE]. CASA slipped to 32.7% from 35.1% in Q4FY26 (roughly flat YoY 32.8%->32.7%) - deposit-franchise quality still well below top-tier private peers (40-45% CASA), a structural NIM constraint [DATA]. CRAR fell to 15.1% from 16.2% YoY [DATA] - comfortably above regulatory minimum but the direction (declining as the book grows) is a watch item. RoA improved to 0.9% (+10bps YoY), RoE to 8.3% (vs 6.6% Q1FY26) - genuine recovery trajectory, management guided 1%+ RoA by FY28, but ROE remains below the ~13% cost-of-equity threshold and below peer private-bank ROEs (mid-teens) [DATA]. SMBC ownership: SMBC holds 20% via a secondary purchase from SBI (13.19%) plus seven domestic banks (6.81%), deal CLOSED May-2025 [DATA - COMPLETED]. RBI approved SMBC to raise its stake to up to 24.99% via letter dated 22-Aug-2025 (approval valid one year, i.e. to ~Aug-2026) and CCI cleared the increase in Sep-2025 [DATA - regulatory approvals COMPLETED; the actual stake increase beyond 20% is still PENDING execution as of latest reporting]; SMBC will not be classified as promoter. On the Q1FY27 call, management (Tonse) said this quarter's corporate growth was driven by Yes Bank's own capabilities rather than the SMBC partnership - i.e. SMBC synergies not yet visible in the P&L [DATA]. Stock fell ~4% on results day despite the beat, even as several brokerages raised target prices by up to 30% - a market/Street disconnect worth flagging, possibly reflecting the CRAR decline or the still-low NIM/ROE base versus a rich multiple [INFERENCE]. Valuation: CMP ~Rs.23.2, P/E ~19.3x, P/B ~1.4x (BVPS ~Rs.16.7, mcap ~Rs.72,849cr) [DATA, screener.in 21-Jul-2026].
recommendation_rationale: No quant score row exists yet for YESBANK in the STOCK_SCORECARD_750 pipeline - per the V1 asymmetric-override rule this defaults to Hold. Nothing in this quarter's disclosure (asset quality improving, SMBC deal progressing through regulatory approvals, no fraud/going-concern/regulatory-action red flag) rises to an escalation-worthy override. On fundamentals alone the picture is genuinely mixed: improving GNPA/NNPA/PCR and a credible RoA-recovery path support a constructive read, but rising credit cost despite improving NPA ratios, declining CASA and CRAR, still sub-cost-of-equity ROE, and a valuation (1.4x P/B) that already prices meaningful further improvement argue against a positive call. Net: Hold, not Sell (no quant trigger to escalate) and not a positive fundamental case either.
summary: YES BANK's Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026) print continued the multi-quarter asset-quality repair story - GNPA 1.3%, NNPA 0.2%, PCR 81.7%, PAT +34% YoY on core NII growth - while NIM (2.7%) and CASA (32.7%, falling sequentially) remain structurally weak versus large private-bank peers, credit cost rose 38.9% YoY despite better headline NPAs, and CRAR eased 110bps YoY to 15.1%. The SMBC ownership overhang is de-risking (20% stake closed May-2025; RBI/CCI have cleared a path to ~25%) but stake increase execution beyond 20% is still pending and management says SMBC synergies aren't yet showing in results. At ~1.4x P/B for a ~7-8% ROE franchise, valuation already leans on continued execution of the RoA-to-1%+ (FY28 guided) path rather than offering a margin of safety.
positive_para: (1) Asset quality has improved for multiple consecutive quarters - GNPA down to 1.3% and NNPA to 0.2% YoY, PCR steady at a healthy 81.7% - this reads as a genuine multi-quarter trend, not a one-off [DATA]. (2) The SMBC stake materially de-risks the governance/ownership overhang that weighed on the stock for years: a marquee foreign strategic anchor now holds 20% (deal closed May-2025) with RBI and CCI both having cleared a path to raise this to ~25% [DATA]. (3) The RoA-recovery trajectory is intact and broad-based - RoA at 0.9% (+10bps YoY), RoE at 8.3% (vs 6.6% a year ago), PAT +34% YoY driven by core NII growth (+17.5-18%) rather than one-off treasury/tax items [DATA].
negative_para: (1) NIM (2.7%) is structurally the lowest among large private banks and the CASA franchise is weakening, not strengthening - 32.7% in Q1FY27 versus 35.1% in Q4FY26 - a structural ceiling on profitability that SMBC capital alone does not fix [DATA]. (2) Credit cost rose 38.9% YoY (provisions Rs.394cr) even as headline NPA ratios improved, and CRAR fell 110bps YoY to 15.1% - capital build is not keeping pace with growth, and the provisioning-quality question needs forensic follow-up before taking the NPA improvement fully at face value [DATA/INFERENCE]. (3) Valuation already reflects much of the hoped-for recovery: 1.4x P/B for a bank still posting sub-cost-of-equity ROE (8.3% vs ~13% COE) leaves little margin of safety, and the stock actually fell ~4% on results day despite the earnings beat - a signal the market may be pricing the same concerns [DATA/INFERENCE].
reverse_dcf_judgment: At CMP ~Rs.23.2 (P/B ~1.4x, BVPS ~Rs.16.7), a simple P/B = ROE/Cost-of-Equity cross-check implies the market is already pricing sustainable ROE in the low-to-mid-teens (near a ~13% COE for an Indian private bank) - i.e. crediting YES BANK with reaching close to its own management-guided 1%+ RoA / low-teens ROE trajectory (targeted by FY28), well ahead of the 8.3% ROE actually being delivered today. This is priced for successful execution of the recovery, not priced cheap against current fundamentals - little margin of safety versus a genuine full-blown reverse-DCF. [INFERENCE - approximate P/B-vs-ROE cross-check only; no multi-year consensus DCF model sourced this pass].
